CCN activation is primarily determined by aerosol size, with variations in chemical effects on activation playing a secondary role.
the ability of aerosol particles to act as cloud condensation nuclei is largely controlled by particle size and that the chemical composition of the particles plays only a secondary role.
the ability of aerosol particles to act as CCNs is largely controlled by particle size, and that the chemical composition plays a secondary role, which varies with the aerosol chemical composition.

the role of aerosols as cloud condensation nuclei.
the chemical composition, size distribution, and mixing state of atmospheric aerosol particles and their impact on cloud formation.
the chemical characterization of atmospheric aerosols in the boundary layer.

the size of aerosols is the main factor determining their CCN activity, and the chemical composition is of secondary importance.
the size distribution determines the CCN concentration and the composition determines the CCN efficiency.

the size distribution of the aerosol is a key factor determining its CCN activity and the CCN activation spectra can be predicted by the size distributions alone, with the exception of a few specific cases, e.g., when the aerosol is dominated by very large particles or particles with a very high hygroscopicity.
size matters more than chemistry for CCN activation.

, in the absence of chemical effects, the CCN activation efficiency is largely determined by the size of particles, with smaller particles having a larger CCN activation efficiency.
the aerosol number concentration and its size distribution, rather than chemical composition, determine the number of cloud condensation nuclei and thus the cloud albedo.
